findings.title: Slow peers never see shared photos
findings.description: `send` now drops a `print` after ten seconds without a key, but `announce` has already recorded that peer in `sentTo`. If the key arrives later, the photo announcement is gone and the catch-up loop skips that peer even on subsequent peer changes.

findings.title: Direct checks fail on working links
findings.description: The `holdKey` wrapper delays public-key messages but lets WebRTC negotiation proceed, while `sendFrame` sends over an open direct channel without requiring that key. If the direct channel opens during the 11-second hold, A2 delivers the print instead of dropping it, and the new browser assertion fails on a working link.

findings.title: Fast re-announcements fail the check
findings.description: The test reads `early` only after `window.__keySent` is set and the held public-key signals have been released. If A2 re-announces and B2 receives the print before the wait and evaluation finish, the test marks the expected post-key delivery as an early arrival and fails.

findings.title: File errors blame the other device
findings.description: The new `sendFile` catch handlers call `gaveUp` for every rejection, although `gaveUp` always says the recipient stopped answering. If reading a file chunk or sending on a direct channel throws instead of timing out, the sender sees that diagnosis and the original error is discarded.
